source.title: Adoption of Fiscal Years 2027 and 2028 Biennial Budget and Fiscal Years 2027-2031 Capital Improvement Program, Exhibit B: FY2027-FY2031 Capital Improvement Program Overview
source.body: City of Berkeley, City Council Special Meeting, June 23, 2026, Item 01 (adopted by resolution)
source.pages: Exhibit B project tables pp.179-229; funding-source tables pp.170, 172-173

capital.adoption_status: The resolution adopts the Five-Year CIP "contained in the City Manager's Proposed" budget "and as amended by subsequent Council action on June 23, 2026" (packet p.6). Exhibit C (pp.249-255) amends FY2027-28 revenues and expenditures by fund; it changes capital grant revenue (funds 305-307, 336, 339) and Measure FF revenue (funds 164, 166) but prints no change to CIP project appropriations. Amendments made from the dais on June 23 are not in this packet; the FY2027 Annual Appropriation Ordinance is the controlling appropriation record and is not yet in BeTH's sources.
caveats: Amounts are budget appropriations and plans, not cash, not expenditures, not encumbrances.

prior_years and fy2026_budget are appropriations already made. Unspent capital appropriations are re-appropriated until a project completes (FY2025 ACFR, Required Supplementary Information budget note); how much of them is unspent or encumbered is not in this source.
Equipment & Fleet is a vehicle replacement schedule of the Equipment Replacement internal service fund (pp.231-247), not project rows; it is summarized in excluded_categories, not itemized.

reconciliation.category_project_counts_match_document: yes, except: Storm Water: The Storm Water tables (pp.210-212) print 13 project titles; p.212 states "14 Projects in Five-Year CIP". Dollar totals tie exactly to the printed Grand Total, so no amount is missing; the stated count is not reproducible.

611.note: Includes 38,660,000 on four Sanitary Sewer rows that print no funding source. The p.170 table attributes all Sanitary Sewer CIP to fund 611; the rows themselves are kept as fund NOT_PRINTED.

streets_139m.question: The $139.3 million figure is the adopted FIVE-YEAR (FY2027-FY2031) Streets CIP budget, not a two-year budget.
streets_139m.cross_check: The July 7, 2026 street plan (Tables 1A-1B) totals the Five-Year Street Rehabilitation Plan at $96,336,212 and the Measure FF five-year street program at $42,119,935 (p.8, Table 4); its fiscal impact section states the combined five-year street CIP "totals over $139 million".

adoption_changes_outside_exhibit_b.note: FY2027 revenue revised from $15,300,000 to $16,651,651 (inflator 4.95% personal income growth). No matching change to Measure FF CIP appropriations is printed.

Grant revenue revised for named capital projects (Codornices Creek, Addison Bicycle Boulevard Phase 2, Adeline, Washington Elementary/Berkeley High, Telegraph Multimodal, West Berkeley/Aquatic Park stormwater).

adoption_changes_outside_exhibit_b.note: Includes $2.5M Oxford for All design, engineering and construction and $150K Addison Street catenary lighting. Exhibit B prints only $150,000 of SOSIP money (Harold Way Placemaking).

reconciliation.to_proposed_presentation: Not reconciled row by row. The earlier extraction of the proposed-CIP presentation (cip-presentation.json) mixes summary labels, funding-source lines and fragments into its project list, so title matching produces false differences. Exhibit B is the proposed CIP that the June 23 resolution adopted; Exhibit C prints no change to CIP project appropriations. cip-presentation.json is kept only as a record of the earlier pass.

answer.question: How much capital funding could Berkeley redirect to streets?
answer.scope: CIP Fund 501 and Measure FF only. Other capital funds (sewer, storm water, zero waste, parks tax, state and county transportation funds, internal service funds) are not yet assessed here.
answer.short_answer: From Measure FF: nothing beyond the adopted plan, without a vote of the people. From CIP Fund 501: at most $2,946,000 of new FY2027-FY2028 appropriations, and only by deferring or cancelling every other project the fund pays for; $10,412,200 of fund 501's FY2027 money (88%) already goes to paving. A one-time amount from unspent carried-over appropriations is possible but cannot be measured from public documents (ceiling at June 30, 2025: $11,568,647, which also funds paving and other projects already under way).
what_would_complete_it: FY2026 year-end fund 501 carryover and encumbrance detail by project.
The FY2027 Annual Appropriation Ordinance (controlling appropriation record, incl. any June 23 amendments).
Public Works and Parks assessments of what deferring each fund 501 project would cost (condition, safety, legal, contracts).
The City's Measure FF maintenance-of-effort calculation and whether FY2027 draws on the Stabilization Reserve.
Restriction research for the other CIP funding sources.

funding_sources.name: Capital Improvement Fund (CIP Fund), fund 501

legal_authority.what: Funded mainly by an annual General Fund transfer. General Fund revenues "may be used for any general government purpose at the discretion of Council."
Appropriated annually through the budget and the Annual Appropriation Ordinance; "Any unused funds are re-appropriated to the following fiscal year until the project is completed."
legal_authority.pages: PDF p.180 (printed p.146), Required Supplementary Information, budgetary basis

legal_authority.what: Council fiscal policy (Resolution 70,456-N.S., July 26, 2022) commits about $8 million a year of General Fund money, inflation-adjusted, to paving; it runs through fund 501 as "Street Rehab PCI Improvements".

funding_sources.permitted_uses: Capital projects as appropriated by Council. No voter or external restriction is identified on the General Fund transfer itself; the restricted portion of the fund balance equals notes receivable (loans), not cash.

classification_june_30_2025.meaning: Assigned = "intended to be used by the City for specific purposes that are neither restricted nor committed through City Council budgetary action ... Intent is expressed by the City Council or City Manager, to which the City Council has delegated the authority." Council can change it without a vote of the people or a new ordinance.
classification_june_30_2025.pages: PDF p.75 (printed p.40); definitions PDF p.103 (printed p.69)

balances_june_30_2025.derivation: assigned 16,060,094 - encumbrances 4,491,447 = 11,568,647. Encumbrances "are reported in assigned fund balance unless the purchase order relates to restricted or committed resources" (ACFR PDF p.180).
balances_june_30_2025.warning: Sixteen months old. The unencumbered amount backs capital appropriations carried forward to FY2026 and is not free money: reassigning it means cancelling or deferring the carried-over projects. FY2026 activity is unaudited until the FY2026 ACFR (expected early 2027).

before_fy2027_prior_years_plus_fy2026.note: Appropriations made, not cash; spent or unspent status is not in the CIP.

appropriations_adopted_cip.pages: pp.172-173 (General Fund Resources incl. CIP Fund) and Exhibit B project tables
appropriations_adopted_cip.city_statement: "current CIP funding is entirely pre-allocated for historical programs such as those in Public Works, there is no CIP funding available for IT in FY 2027 and FY 2028" (budget-adoption p.239).
appropriations_adopted_cip.not_capital: Of the ~$4.95M annual General Fund baseline to the CIP Fund, roughly $4.03M is allocated to capital; the rest goes to personnel, debt service and other costs, and part of the $4.03M is held for supplies, survey consultants and maintenance (budget-adoption p.167).

council_authority.how: By amending the FY2027 Annual Appropriation Ordinance (Council vote). Encumbered amounts are contract obligations and cannot be redirected without changing or cancelling the contracts.
council_authority.limit_paving_floor: Measure FF maintenance of effort: if Council adopts a budget with less than $15.3 million (inflation-adjusted) for street maintenance from non-FF sources, it loses authority to levy Measure FF for two years (BMC 7.11.030(B)). Fund 501 paving is most of that floor. Moving money INTO paving is unconstrained by this; moving it OUT is.

Suspended in a year Council draws $1 million or more from the Stabilization Reserve to adopt a budget, or under a disaster or emergency declaration (7.11.030(D)); reduced if an external street funding source in the 2023-24 budget declines (7.11.030(C)).

maintenance_of_effort.implication: Redirecting non-FF street money elsewhere beyond the headroom would risk about $16.7 million a year of Measure FF. Redirecting other capital INTO streets only adds to the floor.

restrictions.method: restriction_class is taken ONLY from a researched legal_basis in BeTH's 106-fund ledger or a cited statute/measure. Where BeTH's ledger records 'Not yet researched', the class here is 'unknown' and the amount is NOT redirectable for dashboard purposes. classes.voter_approved_tax: Parcel tax, sales tax or similar approved by voters for a stated purpose. Redirection generally requires another vote.
classes.enterprise_fund: Ratepayer money in a self-supporting fund. Generally restricted to the enterprise; Proposition 218 and bond covenants may apply.
classes.internal_service: Charges collected from other City funds to fund a specific service. Not general revenue.
classes.grant_condition: External grant with conditions and clawback risk.
classes.state_restricted: State-allocated revenue with statutory use limits (for example gas tax, vehicle registration fee).
classes.unrestricted: No identified legal restriction. Requires an affirmative citation, never an absence of evidence.
classes.unknown: Not yet researched. DEFAULT. Treated as not redirectable.
classes.council_discretionary: General Fund money appropriated to a capital fund. Council can redirect it by budget action, but encumbered amounts are contracts and paving amounts are bound by the Measure FF maintenance-of-effort floor.

assessment.question: What would it take to bring Berkeley pavement to PCI 60 or better and hold it there?
assessment.answer_status: ANSWERABLE FROM CITY DATA, with limits stated
assessment.finding: The City's own 12-year projections bracket PCI 60. The Five-Year Plan alone is projected to DECLINE to about 56 by 2038. Adding Measure FF is projected to reach about 62 by 2038. So PCI 60+ is, on the City's own modelling, roughly the outcome already purchased by the Plan plus Measure FF, at about $29.6 million a year.
assessment.the_real_gap_is_70_not_60: Berkeley's adopted goal is PCI 70 (BMC 7.11.010(K)(1)), not 60. The City estimates PCI 70 by 2036 requires about $37.6 million a year, roughly $8 million a year more than current plans provide. The funding question Berkeley actually faces is the 62-to-70 gap.

critical_caveats: These are the CITY's projections, not BeTH's. BeTH has not independently verified them and cannot, without the StreetSaver segment data.

PCI 60 as a network AVERAGE can coexist with many streets in failed condition. The City's own goal pairs PCI 70 with "no streets having a PCI below 50". A network average target without a distribution floor can be met while the worst streets decay further.
All figures assume 3% annual construction cost escalation and the Council/Measure FF revenue escalation formulas. The City notes the net effect is a modest real increase in costs relative to funding.
Annual figures are 12-year averages accounting for projected revenue growth, NOT flat annual amounts.
Reaching a level and holding it are different problems with different funding profiles.
assessment.what_beth_adds: Not a rival forecast. BeTH's contribution is to show what the City's own model implies under alternative funding, and to test whether any capital reallocation could close the roughly $8M/yr gap to PCI 70. That test is currently blocked: 0 of 15 CIP funding sources are confirmed redirectable.
